correctness.rationale: For p<B<=p^2, p^2=aB+b has 1<=a<p. Moran membership forces a+b=p, so p(p-1)=a(B-1). Coprimality of a and p gives a|p-1 and hence B=pd+1. The converse digit formula is exact. Harshad membership requires a+b in {1,p,p^2}; these give respectively B=p^2, the Moran family, and an impossible case.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete infinite base spectrum for a natural arithmetic object. It shows that the two-digit Moran bases of p^2 are controlled exactly by the divisor lattice of p-1 and that the Harshad spectrum differs by one canonical base, a structural statement not obtainable from a bounded table alone.
